source.author: verg
source.text: dextera quae Ditis magni sub moenia tendit, hac iter Elysium nobis; at laeva malorum exercet poenas, et ad impia Tartara mittit.
source.text_original: dextera quae Ditis magni sub moenia tendit, / hac iter Elysium nobis; at laeva malorum / exercet poenas, et ad impia Tartara mittit.'
source.text_english: The right hand road, which stretches beneath the walls of mighty Dis, is our way to Elysium; but the left inflicts punishments on the wicked and sends them to impious Tartarus.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: Una est itaque uirtutis ac bonorum uia, quae fert non in Elysios campos, ut poetae loquuntur, sed ad ipsam mundi arcem, at laeua malorum exercet poenas et ad impia Tartara mittit.
reuse.text_original: Una est itaque uirtutis ac bonorum uia, quae fert non in Elysios campos, ut poetae loquuntur, sed ad ipsam mundi arcem, at laeua malorum exercet poenas et ad impia Tartara mittit.
reuse.text_english: Therefore there is one path of virtue and of the good, which leads not to the Elysian fields, as the poets say, but to the very citadel of the world; while the left-hand path inflicts the punishments of evils and sends men to impious Tartarus.
